claims.reason: The binder is the theorem's own instance argument. It is used only to elaborate `limit.π F i`, and instance search finds `HasLimit F` globally: `TopCat.topCat_hasLimitsOfSize [UnivLE.{v, u}] : HasLimitsOfSize.{w, v} TopCat.{u}` (Mathlib/Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Basic.lean:173), used with u := max v u. `UnivLE.{v, max v u}` is synthesized via `univLE_of_max` (Mathlib/Basic/UnivLE.lean:74; line 77 checks `example : UnivLE.{v, max v u} := inferInstance`). A SmallCategory on `J : Type v` has morphisms in Type v, so the standard instances give HasLimitsOfShape J and then HasLimit F. `topCat_hasLimitsOfShape J [Small.{max v u} J]` (line 167) is an alternative route. The library itself uses the concrete `TopCat.limitCone F` for `F : J ⥤ TopCat.{max v u}` with no limit assumption (Limits.lean:451). Deleting the binder changes nothing else in the statement. The proof term still works, because `limitCylinder_subset_iff_eventually` applies to any cone with `IsLimit`, here `limit.cone F` / `limit.isLimit F` from the global instance.
